findings.F1: During 6-day rises on days of above-average volume, the 3-day excess return over holding grows with the 6-day return measured in 20-day daily volatility: the top tercile of that run strength is followed by +2.43 % (t 3.37 with one day's cases taken together, 713 cases, strength 0.238), the middle tercile by +0.24 % (t 0.51, 712 cases) and the bottom tercile by −0.16 % (t −0.36, 713 cases).
findings.F2: Across all grid bars, the 6-day return deciles show the same direction but weaker: the top decile (6-day rise above 15 %) is followed by +0.94 % 3-day excess (t 1.55, 1156 cases), and the deciles between −2 % and +5 % sit between −0.79 % and −0.04 %.
findings.F3: Inside 6-day rises, the day's range against its 20-day average range carries the volume signal's information: the widest-range quintile is followed by +1.34 % 3-day excess (t 2.13, 1005 cases, strength 0.130), the other four quintiles lie between −0.19 % and +0.22 %. Taken together in one regression, neither log volume ratio (t 1.11) nor log range ratio (t 1.24) stands alone.
findings.F4: Volume adds nothing outside up runs: in 6-day falls the volume-ratio quintiles are followed by 3-day excess returns from −0.66 % to +0.14 %, all with |t| ≤ 1.43, and the joint volume t is −0.85.
findings.F5: The heavy-volume up-run effect is unstable by year: its 3-day excess is negative in 2018 (−2.27 %, 91 cases), 2022 (−0.64 %, 222) and 2025 (−0.95 %, 340), and positive in the other five years (up to +2.81 % in 2021, 254 cases), so it pays in bull years.
findings.F6: The book's gain is concentrated in rare days: its days above its own 95th percentile (+1.61 %) sum to 211 % of its total summed daily gain. Its daily returns correlate 0.59 with the coins' daily returns.
findings.F7: The brief's own pattern points the other way but cannot be told from chance: wide-range (over 1.5 times the 20-day average range), flat-body days after a 6-day rise are followed by +1.84 % 3-day excess (t 1.56, 107 cases), not by a move back.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 6-day rise measured in units of its own daily volatility over the past 20 days, the larger its further rise over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A rise that is strong for the coin's usual volatility is a reason to stay long for 3 more days, and a rise that is weak for that volatility is a reason not to.
ideas.name: vol-scaled run strength continues

ideas.idea: While a coin has risen over the past 6 days, the wider a day's high-to-low range compared with its average daily range over the past 20 days, the larger the coin's further rise over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A wide-range day inside an up-run is a reason to stay long for 3 more days, and a narrow-range day in the same run is a reason not to.
ideas.name: wide range extends up-run
